title: Verifier-Guided Repair Improves LLM-Generated Vendor CLI Configurations: A Preregistered Controlled Fault-Injection Paired Study
abstract: We report a preregistered controlled-challenge paired experiment that tests whether exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow reduces residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair. Under the hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 adapter and shared_controlled_fault_candidate pairing semantics (preregistration vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1), we executed 40 planned task indices and observed 39 complete pairs (one source generation invalid and excluded per the preregistered rule). Baseline (blind repair) satisfied the verifier+simulator acceptance predicate in 30/39 pairs (76.92%); guarded (verifier-guided) satisfied it in 38/39 pairs (97.44%). Paired counts: n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. The paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points); two-sided exact paired test p = 0.021484375; 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Confirmatory execution used the declared model version gpt-5-mini and consumed 118 hosted-model calls (<= budget 120). The preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair aggregation was not present in the archived confirmatory summary and therefore remains unresolved for confirmatory inference; the frozen harmful-change mapping and per-episode validator traces were recorded and enable deterministic independent recomputation. We present the preregistered primary result, clarify execution semantics, describe observed failure modes from archived traces, and state limitations and reproducibility guidance.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed as automation aids for network operations (NetOps) tasks such as intent-to-configuration translation and automated remediation. A common safety architecture is generate–verify–repair (GVR): a candidate artifact is produced, deterministically checked by a verifier, and, if violations occur, verifier diagnostics are fed back to a generator/repair model to produce a corrected candidate. Prior empirical work in code and Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) settings reports verifier-mediated improvements in verifier-detected pass rates while also documenting new failure modes (e.g., verifier-exploitation) and interaction costs [see Related Work]. However, controlled paired evidence that isolates the effect of exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics on vendor CLI configuration repair is sparse. Deterministic verifier diagnostics can only affect outcomes when initial candidates trigger actionable diagnostics; to guarantee activation in a confirmatory design we used preregistered deterministic controlled faults and a shared-candidate paired design that reuses the identical injected-fault candidate across arms. Our primary research question is: does exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow reduce residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair, under matched repair budgets and matched source-generation?
sections.related_work: Empirical evaluations of verifier-guided workflows concentrate in code, IaC, and DSL domains where deterministic verifiers are available. Controlled pipeline evaluations show that inserting verifiers between generation and acceptance tends to raise verifier pass rates and that feeding diagnostics to a repair model increases the chance a corrected artifact satisfies the verifier on recheck [F1,F2]. Complementary studies emphasize caveats: single-proxy iterative refinement can be exploited (optimization toward the verifier proxy producing target-property degradations) and verifier-mediated pipelines impose a "verifier tax" in interaction and compute cost that depends on horizon and design [F3,F4]. Survey and field studies specific to NetOps indicate helpfulness for read-oriented assistance but warn against assuming safe closed-loop autonomous changes without careful verification and governance [F5]. These lines motivate a controlled, deterministic fault-injection paired experiment that (a) ensures intervention activation, (b) measures the paired effect of exposing diagnostics while matching source generations and repair budgets, and (c) records the full per-episode verifier traces required to audit safety aggregations such as harmful over-repair.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered (vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1). The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline: the difference in proportions of task pairs where the post-repair candidate satisfies the joint acceptance predicate (deterministic vendor-CLI verifier AND simulator-based compliance check).

Adapter, pairing, and treatment semantics. Confirmatory execution used the hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 adapter under its shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics. Under this contract each task index received exactly one deterministically injected controlled-fault candidate which was reused unchanged across both experimental conditions; exactly one sampled initial generation per task pair was performed and reused by both arms. Baseline denotes blind repair (repair without exposure of validator diagnostics) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. With these semantics both arms share the same initial candidate and receive their permitted repair opportunity; therefore observed cross-arm differences isolate the effect of exposing diagnostics under a matched repair budget and matched source generation.

Model sampling and runtime parameters. The declared model used for confirmatory execution was gpt-5-mini. The archived model configuration records temperature = null (unset); null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Exactly one sampled initial generation per pair was reused by both arms; the design does not measure effects of independent first-pass sampling across conditions.

Controlled-challenge task bank and primary acceptance predicate. We used a deterministic controlled-fault generator to create 40 preregistered task indices with realistic, actionable violations injected into vendor-CLI templates (examples: dropped-required-restore patterns, protected-interface changes, paired-MTU-change patterns). The primary success predicate required agreement between a deterministic vendor-CLI validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) and a simulator-based compliance check; both components were executed and their combined agreement defines the binary success flag used in the confirmatory test. A harmful-change labeling mapping (frozen before execution) operationally marks an episode as harmful if post-repair validator traces include codes such as PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE or UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE; that mapping and the per-episode validation traces were recorded during execution and permit deterministic recomputation of the preregistered harmful-overrepair statistic, but that aggregation was not produced in the archived confirmatory summary and thus is unresolved for confirmatory inference here.

Statistical analysis plan and runtime bookkeeping. The preregistered primary test is a two-sided exact paired binary test (exact McNemar or equivalent). We report discordant-pair counts (n10, n01), the absolute paired risk difference with a 95% paired-bootstrap percentile confidence interval (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729), and the two-sided exact p-value. Missingness handling followed the preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' rule (exclude a pair only if both executions are unscorable); a prespecified sensitivity plan treats missing episodes as failures. All per-episode traces and scored artifacts required to reproduce aggregations were recorded and archived.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. Planned confirmatory pairs = 40; completed episodes correspond to 39 complete pairs (one source generation invalid and excluded under the preregistered rule). Hosted-model calls consumed = 118 (<= planned maximum 120). Source-generation attempts = 40 (source_valid_count = 39; source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1).

Primary confirmatory outcomes (complete_pairs = 39). Baseline (blind repair) success = 30/39 = 0.7692307692307693. Guarded (verifier-guided) success = 38/39 = 0.9743589743589743. Paired contingency counts (guarded, baseline): n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points). Exact two-sided paired test (McNemar exact): p = 0.021484375. 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, bootstrap_seed = 1729).

Missingness and exclusions. One pair was excluded by the preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' rule because the source generation was invalid/unscorable; terminal error reasons were recorded in the execution manifest.

Representative failure-mode traces. Archived per-episode validator traces document distinct failure modes that the guarded workflow addressed in multiple discordant pairs. Representative archived examples include: (1) dropped_required_restore pattern where a required final "restore admin up" command was omitted from the injected candidate and later restored by the guarded repair (task-000001 traces); (2) protected_interface_change where an injected fault modifies a protected management interface (mgmt1) that must not change and where guarded diagnostics led to repairs that avoided touching the protected interface while blind repair sometimes left the protected change in place (task-000002/000003 traces); and (3) paired-link atomic MTU-change patterns where sequence constraints (both interfaces down before MTU edits) are required and where diagnostics helped the model restore the required sequence. These concrete trace examples (execution/scoring artifacts task-000001..task-000003) illustrate the sorts of verifier-identified violations that, when exposed, can drive targeted corrective edits. The archived artifacts contain the full per-episode validator feedback, final_configuration texts, and violation_codes for deterministic independent inspection.
sections.discussion:
Magnitude, discordant-structure, and mechanism. The observed paired improvement (~+20.5 percentage points) is driven predominantly by guarded-only successes (n10 = 9) versus a single baseline-only success (n01 = 1). Because the adapter pairing semantics guarantee that both arms received the same shared initial candidate and matched repair budgets, this discordant structure attributes the bulk of the confirmatory effect to exposing deterministic validator diagnostics to the repair model rather than to differences in the source generation or repair-call budget. Archived validator_trace.violation_codes and normalized_configuration fields show that diagnostics frequently identify precise offending fields (e.g., FINAL_STATE_MISMATCH, PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE, UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE) and that guarded episodes' repairs often remove or reorder only the minimal commands needed to satisfy the verifier+simulator predicate. The representative artifacts (task-000001..task-000003) make this mechanism concrete: diagnostics highlighting a missing restore or a protected-interface edit appear to steer repairs away from harmful edits or toward required restore commands.

Uncertainty, power, and ceiling effects. With complete_pairs = 39 the primary two-sided exact test yields p = 0.0215 and a 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI that excludes zero. Precision remains limited for subgroup or per-fault-class inference: the sample size yields reasonable sensitivity to the observed magnitude but provides limited power to detect smaller effects or to estimate per-class differences precisely. Additionally, the observed guarded success rate (97.44%) approaches the practical ceiling of verifier+simulator agreement in this controlled task bank; ceiling proximity reduces headroom for further absolute gains and complicates interpretation of marginal improvements in higher-fidelity deployments.

Harmful-overrepair safety aggregation—status and implications. The preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair aggregation (bounded-safety hypothesis) was not present in the archived confirmatory summary produced by the confirmatory analysis executor, and therefore we do not present a confirmatory safety verdict in this paper. The frozen harmful-change mapping (episodes flagged as harmful when post-repair validator traces include PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE or UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE) and the per-episode validator traces needed to compute that aggregation were recorded during execution; independent auditors can deterministically recompute the preregistered harmful-overrepair statistic from the archived artifacts. Until such recomputation appears in a confirmatory artifact, any harmful-overrepair numbers computed outside the archived confirmatory summary should be treated as exploratory, not confirmatory.

Operational implications and verifier tax. Guarded repair materially increased verifier+simulator-validated correctness on this controlled fault bank, but it required additional interactions: confirmatory execution consumed 118 hosted-model calls under the matched budget. While those counts permit exploratory cost-per-avoided-failure calculations, large-scale operational feasibility (latency, monetary cost, and human-triage tradeoffs) requires deployment-scale measurement. We therefore avoid operational claims about reduced triage time or deployment risk that were not directly measured.

Verifier-exploitation and generality. Short-horizon, single-repair budgets and the paired shared-candidate design reduce exposure to long-horizon verifier-exploitation pathologies that have been documented elsewhere. Nevertheless, verifier-exploitation remains a conceptual risk in multi-step agentic pipelines. Mitigations include multi-verifier ensembles, explicit harmful-change constraints (the frozen harmful-change mapping is one example), calibrated abstention, and uncertainty quantification. Generalization beyond this synthetic vendor-CLI bank, the declared model (gpt-5-mini), and the deterministic validator and simulator used here remains to be demonstrated.
sections.conclusion: In this preregistered controlled-challenge paired experiment using the hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 adapter and shared controlled-fault candidates, exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow produced a statistically detectable, substantial increase in verifier+simulator-validated configuration success (approx. +20.51 percentage points; p = 0.021484375; 95% CI [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359]). The finding is bounded to the preregistered synthetic task bank, the declared model gpt-5-mini, and the deterministic verifier and simulator used in execution. The preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test was not produced in the archived confirmatory summary and therefore remains unresolved for confirmatory inference; the frozen harmful-change mapping and per-episode validation traces recorded during execution provide exact inputs for independent reconstruction of that safety statistic. We recommend multi-model, multi-verifier replications, explicit inclusion of the preregistered harmful-overrepair confirmatory aggregation in future confirmatory analyses, and larger-scale cost/latency studies to assess operational feasibility and safety at NetOps scale.

disclosure_statement: Preregistration: vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1. Adapter family used for confirmatory execution: hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2. Declared model used for confirmatory execution: gpt-5-mini. Exact initial master prompt archived as provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: f781dd7978328198146d586cf33e0f4b783c8db126bd0f16fcd13699455ebb10). Human role and autonomy boundary: a Research Director selected the topic family and pre-lock constraints; after the autonomy lock the autonomous system performed literature verification, preregistration, experiment execution, analysis, and manuscript generation; no manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the lock. Execution semantics: the archived model configuration records temperature = null (unset); null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Pairing semantics: exactly one sampled initial generation per task pair was performed and reused by both arms under shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics; baseline denotes blind repair (no validator diagnostics exposed) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. The preregistered harmful-change labeling mapping used to define the planned safety aggregation was frozen before execution; the mapping and per-episode validation traces required to compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation were recorded during execution. All per-episode traces, scored artifacts, and transformation mappings needed to reproduce the preregistered secondary aggregations were recorded in the archived evidence bundle. The study followed the preregistered stopping rule.
limitations: Synthetic controlled-fault task bank: tasks were deterministically injected and do not represent a broad naturalistic distribution of production NetOps incidents; external validity to live operator workloads is limited.
Single-model and single-adapter evaluation: confirmatory execution used only the declared model gpt-5-mini and one adapter family; results do not establish multi-model generality.
Simulator-backed primary success predicate: primary success required agreement of deterministic verifier and simulator; simulator fidelity and verifier coverage constrain construct validity.

Sample size and power: complete_pairs = 39 provides detectable effects of the observed magnitude but limits precision for subgroup and per-fault-class inference; exploratory subgroup analyses are not confirmatory.
Operational cost/latency unresolved for deployment: execution was instrumented and counts were recorded, but large-scale operational feasibility (verifier tax tradeoffs) requires larger-scale study.

Verifier-exploitation and long-horizon agentic pathologies remain possible: this controlled setting mitigates some risks, but broader agentic workflows need additional defenses (multi-verifier designs, calibrated abstention, uncertainty quantification).

Preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test not present in archived confirmatory summary: the archived confirmatory analysis executor did not compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation; the per-episode traces and the frozen mapping required to compute it were recorded and are available for independent reaggregation, but the preregistered confirmatory safety verdict is therefore unresolved in this paper.
